_readme: Address hypotheses for roms/zelda_la_dx.gbc (gitignored, not versioned). Each entry: value/meaning, source tier, verified_count, confidence. Hardware-standard GB addresses (OAM, PPU registers) are high-confidence by architecture, not empirical hypotheses -- still logged here since the driver reads them the same way.

oam_base.meaning: 40 sprites x 4 bytes (Y, X, tile, flags); Y<160 && Y>0 means on-screen
oam_base.note: Link has NO fixed slot -- game reassigns which slot renders him between frames (confirmed session 2: same moving sprite pair seen at slot 16/17 then slot 2/3). find_link() works around this by excluding known-stationary NPC (Y,X) rather than tracking a slot.

dialogue_text_scratch_line1.meaning: Fixed scratch-buffer tile-ID range reused for dialogue line 1, regardless of speaker/content
dialogue_text_scratch_line1.note: Confirmed byte-for-byte identical across 2 different NPCs with different text -- see docs/CONCEPT.md. Decode by pixel bitmap, never by this ID.

link_position_x.meaning: Link's X coordinate, world/screen pixel units
link_position_x.note: From villager_screen checkpoint: +1/+2 per RIGHT tap (4x), -1/-2 per LEFT tap (4x), flat across 4x DOWN + 4x UP taps. Matches the community LADX disassembly's hLinkPositionX hypothesis exactly. Supersedes the OAM-based find_link() workaround as the primary position source -- see DECISIONS.md.

link_position_x_shadow.meaning: Tracks link_position_x byte-for-byte (same deltas on every RIGHT/LEFT tap) -- purpose unconfirmed (double-buffer? sub-pixel-free copy?)
link_position_x_shadow.note: Found alongside 0xFF98 in the same full-space diff; identical delta sequence on all 8 taps (4 RIGHT + 4 LEFT). Not yet needed by any consumer -- logged for completeness.

link_position_y.meaning: Link's Y coordinate, world/screen pixel units
link_position_y.note: +1/+2 per DOWN tap (4x), -1/-2 per UP tap (4x), flat across 4x RIGHT + 4x LEFT taps. Matches hLinkPositionY hypothesis.

link_direction.meaning: Facing direction, small enum (1=right seen at spawn, 3=down, 2=up observed; 0 seen transiently mid-turn)
link_direction.note: Changed exactly on a direction change (RIGHT->DOWN->UP), stable while repeating the same direction. Left-value not yet observed directly -- infer from the enum pattern, don't assume without a dedicated LEFT-only check.

room_id.meaning: Current room/screen identifier -- NOT globally unique by itself, see collision below
room_id.note: front_yard=162, overworld_screen2=178, villager_screen=177, screen3_north=161, shop_screen=179, house2_interior=169, starting_house=163 (map_id=16), room160=160/map0 (west of 161, exits mapped, content corrected -- see world_topology.room160_exits_and_content), room176=176/map0 (south of room160, exits + 2 NPCs confirmed -- see world_topology.room176_exits_and_content), room192=192/map0 (new, south of room176, unexplored), room250=250/map29 (new interior, through room176's building door, unexplored). COLLISION found September 8, 2026 (Explorer subagent, exploring east of front_yard, observed twice independently in separate script runs): a new outdoor room directly east of front_yard also reads room_id=163, but map_id=0 -- distinct from starting_house's map_id=16 at the same room_id. (room_id, map_id) is the real key, room_id alone is not. room_id=177/map_id=0 re-confirmed September 8, 2026 via real navigation (front_yard_to_room177 below), matching legacy's old villager_screen checkpoint's room_id. Supersedes ScreenGrid's discovery-order screen names as the canonical room key -- see DECISIONS.md.

map_id.meaning: Coarser than room_id -- looks like an overworld/interior (or dungeon) discriminator, not a full map index. Combined with room_id, forms the actual unique room key -- see room_id's note above.
map_id.note: 0 on every overworld screen checked (7, now including the 3 new rooms west/east/south of front_yard), 16 on the one interior (house2_interior/starting_house). Only 2 distinct values seen so far -- can't yet distinguish 'overworld' from 'a specific interior/dungeon number' with just one interior sample.

link_position.ruled_out_reason: Isolated via 4x consistent-small-positive-delta diff on RIGHT taps (strong signal, see method below), but a follow-up RIGHT/LEFT/DOWN cross-check showed all 4 increase on every tap regardless of direction -- animation-frame or step counters, not an (X,Y) coordinate. A true X byte would decrease on LEFT; none did.
link_position.method_for_next_attempt: This WRAM-only search (0xC000-0xDFFF) was the mistake: the review docs/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md flagged that neither memory hunt had ever scanned HRAM (0xFF80-0xFFFE). A full 0x0000-0xFFFF diff (see legacy/game_agents/experiments/ram_diff_hram.rb and its ram_diff_hram2.rb cross-validation follow-up) found the real coordinates there in one pass. The same full-space-diff technique is what the terrain-collision-in-WRAM question should reuse.
link_position.accepted_workaround: OBSOLETE now that hram.link_position_x/y are verified -- kept as history, not to be reused. find_link() via OAM exclusion was sufficient for the mapping tool but is exactly the wrong-layer approach the review calls out.

link_health.status: candidate found, September 10 2026 (Explorer session, bed-healing test in house2_interior)
link_health.meaning: Current HP, in eighth-heart units (8 units/heart -- 3 heart containers -> 24 = full)
link_health.companion_meaning: Heart containers (max hearts), plain integer -- read as 3 everywhere checked so far
link_health.note: First surfaced incidentally in dialogues.starting_house_npc_beds's note ('HUD hearts (0xDB5A) read 24 before and after') -- promoted here with its own entry since it's directly reusable for any future damage-tracking work, not just that one dialogue check. This session's own direct reads corroborate it independently: (1) loaded lib_house2_interior.dump fresh (different method: direct checkpoint load + read, not an incidental note during a dialogue test) -- 0xDB5A=24, 0xDB5B=3, matching a rendered screenshot showing exactly 3 solid hearts; (2) read 0xDB5A on 4 already-saved checkpoints from 2 OTHER past sessions (riverside_south/225-226 area) that had logged their own HP informally as fractions out of 20 in their prose -- lib_225_ne_shield_held_end.dump (logged '20/20') read 0xDB5A=20; lib_226_retreat_end.dump, lib_226_up2_end.dump and lib_224_down_end.dump (all logged '4/20', the room cluster's low-health floor) all read 0xDB5A=4. Exact match to those sessions' own independently-logged numbers, across 2 different past sessions and real in-game damage events (not just re-reading a static full-HP state) -- satisfies AGENTS.md's verified_count>=2 bar (genuinely independent checks, different sessions AND a different method). CAVEAT found this session: a raw mmu.write(0xDB5A, ...) does NOT by itself update the visible HUD heart icons, even after 120 idle frames -- the on-screen hearts are apparently only redrawn by the game's own HP-changing code path (e.g. taking real damage), not read live from this address every frame. So this byte is confirmed to track real HP faithfully through organic gameplay changes, but a direct write to it is invisible on screen until/unless some in-game routine touches HP again -- useful to know before using it as a manufactured-low-HP testing shortcut in a future session.

equipped_b_item.status: candidate found, September 11 2026 (Builder task implementing DECISIONS.md's D13)
equipped_b_item.meaning: Equipped B-slot item ID -- 0 observed on a fresh pre-shield boot, 4 on every post-shield checkpoint sampled (the only inventory change ever observed in this project, Tarin's Level-1 Shield gift). Not confirmed against an external item-ID table -- the value-to-item mapping is inferred solely from being the one observed transition, not cross-checked.

equipped_b_item.note: Diffed WRAM (0xC000-0xDFFF) between a fresh boot_fresh() pre-shield state and lib_after_shield_interior.dump, keeping only bytes that changed AND read identically on 2 more post-shield checkpoints (lib_front_yard.dump, lib_226_explore_start.dump) -- 0xDB00 was the only candidate in the DB0x/item-adjacent range (197 total candidates in the full diff, mostly HUD/text-buffer/animation-table noise elsewhere). Independently re-checked (same script, same session) on 5 more checkpoints spanning lib_villager_screen/house2_interior/224_explore_start/225_ne_shield_held_end/e209b_entry_verified -- all read 0xDB00=4, regardless of room/HP/position. This is one session's own correlation method only (not a second, genuinely independent session or method per AGENTS.md's verified_count>=2 bar) -- a future session confirming this via the pause-menu item wheel (SELECT-cycling and watching the byte change in lockstep with the HUD icon), or once a second inventory item exists to contrast against, would promote this to verified. Consumed by lib/navigator.rb's Navigator.shield_equipped? (SHIELD_ITEM_ID = 4) for D13's hostile-avoidance primitive.

intro_door_gate.status: RESOLVED 2026-09-08 -- confirmed legitimate shield-gating, not a bug. Not a RAM address entry; kept here for provenance continuity with the investigation above.
intro_door_gate.note: Confirmed, not just hypothesized: got the shield through a real conversation with Tarkin (lib/navigator.rb, D7) and walked to the south door -- zero blocking, zero 'Hé mon gars' message. The door was always legitimately shield-gated; front_yard's approach to Tarkin (target y:80,x:112) had been abandoned early by a known legacy/ bug (root_cause_2026_09_07_night below), so the shield was never obtained and the block looked like a mystery gate. The 0xD3E7/0xDFF9 flags recorded in the previous entry (method_2026_09_07_evening, kept below for the record) were noise from the door NPC's dialogue box opening, as suspected -- not re-examined further, no longer relevant now the real mechanism is confirmed.
intro_door_gate.root_cause_2026_09_07_night: Checked Link's actual OAM position against the two stationary NPCs at the before_shield_gift checkpoint (reading via MMU#debug_read, gemboy PR #9, to bypass a PPU-bus-gating artifact that made legacy/primitives.rb's oam_sprites return an empty list at this exact frame): Link at (74,82)/(74,90), the likely-Tarkin NPC pair at (80,120)/(80,128) -- a 38px gap, nowhere near adjacent. front_yard's approach loops break early because move_tiles's own 'moved' count under-reports: 6 manual :right taps from this checkpoint each returned moved=0 while x visibly advanced by 2px per tap (82->84->86->...->94) -- the long-documented 'creeping collision' undercount (see scenarios.rb's house2_interior comment for the same pattern elsewhere). front_yard's loops treat moved=0 as 'blocked, try something else' and give up on approaching Tarkin long before actually reaching him. No shield is ever given; the door NPC blocking Link afterward is correct game logic, not a bug or a gate to bypass.
intro_door_gate.method_2026_09_07_evening_superseded: Isolated the door-block trigger itself (proximity-based, fires at y=122->121 with a backward reposition, dialogue 'Hé mon gars, attends un peu !') and diffed WRAM+HRAM+OAM+IO around it: 195 bytes changed, mostly dialogue-render state (0xD500-0xD616, matching wram_unmapped.room_object_grid's earlier same-room diff) and audio registers. Flagged 0xD3E7/0xDFF9 as gate-condition candidates -- superseded by the same-night finding above: this dialogue is the door NPC correctly reacting to Link not having the shield, not a special gate state.
intro_door_gate.not_worth_fixing_in_legacy: D5 says legacy/ is replaced, not extended; move_tiles's creeping-collision undercount is exactly the class of primitive D7's snapshot-based tool is meant to replace properly. Reaching Tarkin is deferred to Session 2's new lib/ navigation tool rather than patched here.

room_object_grid.status: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-08 -- the signal exists, but in VRAM's existing BG tilemap, not a separate WRAM buffer. See terrain_collision.background_tilemap_predicts_walkability below.
room_object_grid.note: Session 1 hypothesis (docs/ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md's next question): a per-room 16x16 object grid in WRAM whose type-per-cell predicts collision. Brute-forced every (base address in 0xC000-0xDFFF, stride in [8,9,10,16,20], row-major/col-major) against the starting_house oracle grid (legacy/.../screen_maps/starting_house.json, 32 cells with edges, 123 direction-edge samples, 28 blocked/95 ok) using a single-byte-value classifier. Best candidates: 80.5% accuracy vs a 77.2% majority-class baseline, using degenerate marker values (0, 255) that are common noise anywhere in RAM -- not a credible signal.
room_object_grid.why_inconclusive_not_refuted: Tested against only one room (front_yard, the second room the criterion calls for, is blocked -- see intro_door_gate's related_finding above). A single static snapshot can't isolate a candidate the way D1's method did (diff between two different rooms to find the block that changes); with only one room, most of WRAM is trivially 'consistent' with almost any single-cell hypothesis by chance. Re-test once a second room is reachable, using the diff-between-rooms method NEXT.md originally specified, before concluding either way on D4.

save_and_continue_mechanic.status: confirmed, fully -- coordinating session, September 8, 2026, direct mechanical verification of room176's two NPC dialogue lines (dialogues.room176_pair_a/room176_pair_b), not trusted on their word alone.
save_and_continue_mechanic.note:
Holding A+B+START+SELECT together for ~120 frames (not a single tap -- needs sustained hold) opens a pause/save menu, confirmed by rendered text: 'REVENIR AU JEU' / 'SAUVEGARDER & QUITTER'. Selecting the second option (down, then A) triggers a REAL battery-RAM save -- gemboy/roms/zelda_la_dx.sav's MD5 and mtime both changed after the sequence (721d34c...->32aa1da..., confirmed via direct file diff, not just a WRAM/state guess). This writes real Game Boy save data, no ROM content -- see the copyright note in DECISIONS.md-adjacent discussion, this is safe to persist/commit unlike a Motherboard#dump checkpoint (which embeds the full ROM via MBC1/5's @rom = cartridge.rom_bytes).
Second claim also verified: rebooting the ROM fresh with this .sav present (via CartridgeLoader/build_emulator, the normal boot path, not a Marshal checkpoint) and skipping the title sequence (periodic :start taps) resumes at (80,124) in room_id=250/map_id=29 -- the crate interior where the save was made, right at its own door threshold, NOT the exact mid-room position where the save was triggered (80,116 on entry, drifted further during testing). Confirms room176_pair_b's claim: continuing resumes at 'the last door passed through', not a pixel-exact save point.
Practical implication for this project's continuous-save design (see NEXT.md): the game's own .sav is a genuine, small (32768 bytes), ROM-free save mechanism -- a real alternative/complement to the in-process main.dump for any future need to persist progress durably (e.g. across a fresh container), once real story/item progress (not just topology mapping) is worth preserving that way.

select_map_screen.status: confirmed and substantially corrected -- isolated Explorer subagent, September 8, 2026, full-BG-tilemap MD5 hashing frame-by-frame (far more precise than the original pixel-eyeball check). CORRECTION to this entry's first version: holding :select does NOT produce a stable held-open state. It's an automatic cycle -- ~20 frames initial delay, then repeating ~36 frames open / ~60 frames closed (~96-frame period, ~1.6s), independent of any input. The first check's screenshot only happened to land inside an open window.
select_map_screen.note:
REFUTED: panning. 150 frames of full-tilemap hashing under 5 conditions (select-only control, select+each direction pressed once mid-open-window) -- left/right show zero divergence from control; up/down only ever diverge because the held direction leaks into real gameplay once the overlay auto-closes (down's divergence matches the already-known front_yard->178 exit). No scrolled/panned grid state ever observed. No camera-pan mechanic exists.
REFUTED: visual discovery-status encoding. The grid is 16x16 raw BG tiles (tilemap rows 1-16, cols 2-17; SCX=SCY=0 confirmed so tile coords map 1:1 to screen). In front_yard's stable open state, 255 of 256 interior cells are the identical tile (0x2c) -- only exception is the 'you are here' marker itself. No visual trace of the ~7 rooms already visited by this point in the project.
REFUTED (negative result, not proof of absence): a bulk per-cell WRAM structure. Full 8KB WRAM diff (0xC000-0xDFFF) between closed and stable-open states: only 115 bytes changed, largest contiguous run 15 bytes -- nowhere near a 256-cell bitmap. Doesn't rule out a structure written once elsewhere (e.g. at room-entry) and merely read here, only that opening the screen itself doesn't touch one in bulk.
CONFIRMED: the '!?' icon is a fixed, room/position-independent legend -- byte-for-byte identical tilemap region (rows 6-9, cols 20-31) in both front_yard and room177, two different rooms/positions.
INCONCLUSIVE: the 'you are here' marker's exact semantics. Its grid cell (interior row10/col2) was IDENTICAL between front_yard and room177 -- two different physical rooms -- which is not what a real position tracker would be expected to do; needs a checkpoint further from front_yard to settle whether it's a fixed 'home' indicator or something else. Its surrounding tile pattern does differ per checkpoint (front_yard: 1 tile; room177: 3 tiles; room160: a different 3-tile arrangement), each stable within its own open window (not a blink-phase artifact) -- real per-checkpoint differences, not yet explained.
TWO UNEXPLAINED ANOMALIES, flagged not chased further (low priority): (1) starting_house (an interior) never reached the grid-open tilemap signature across a 300-frame scan -- plausibly the map is genuinely disabled indoors, a real finding, but only one data point, not confirmed with a second interior. (2) room160 reaches a grid-LIKE tilemap signature (uniform 0x2c body) but renders as a blank field with no grid lines and a completely different icon-region tile set -- most plausible hypothesis (not confirmed): the map's grid-line/icon graphics borrow CHR tile slots from whatever tileset the current room has loaded, so appearance can be room-tileset-dependent even when the tilemap's structural state matches (confirmed DMG mode, not a CGB VRAM-bank artifact).
Bottom line for future use: this is not the world-topology shortcut it looked like at first glance -- no pan, no visible fog-of-war, no bulk-readable structure found. Still useful as a confirmed 'this room has X neighbors within one screen' sanity check via the marker/icon, and the two anomalies (no map indoors, room-dependent rendering) are genuine unexplained facts worth remembering.
NEW LEAD, September 8, 2026 (dialogues.crate_room_book_a, an in-game hint text): the map screen has a d-pad-movable CURSOR, distinct from the already-refuted viewport panning -- moving the cursor and pressing :a is described as showing the place name and an 'owl message' per location. Never tested (the panning test moved the whole view, not a cursor). If real, this could reveal room names/hints without physically visiting them -- worth a dedicated session moving the cursor deliberately during an open window and checking for new UI elements or a WRAM/tilemap change localized to the cursor's own tile.
SECOND DATA POINT, September 9 2026 (live re-check from lib_shop_screen.dump, an interior, frame-by-frame capture during the open window): the map DOES render here -- not disabled indoors in general, narrowing anomaly (1) to starting_house specifically, not interiors as a class -- but the outer dotted border and a position marker are present while the interior grid LINES and the '!?' legend icon are both absent. Same room-dependent partial-rendering pattern as anomaly (2) (room160), now seen in a second, different room -- strengthens the room-tileset-dependent-rendering hypothesis without fully explaining it. The cursor+owl-message lead above remains the untested next step and the most likely way to learn whether this screen is actually useful once interacted with, rather than just viewed.
THIRD SESSION, September 9 2026 (this session -- the cursor+owl-message lead above, tested directly): MIXED RESULT, not a clean confirm/refute -- pressing A IS real and reveals a genuine, previously-undocumented UI element, but the d-pad-cursor claim specifically did not hold up under testing.
CONFIRMED: holding (not tapping) :a for ~20+ frames during an open window opens a real modal text box, distinct from the base grid -- rows 1-5 of the tilemap (interior columns 1-18) get overwritten with a blank-fill tile (0x7e) plus a typewriter-rendered line of glyph tiles (front_yard: 16 characters starting at tile ID 0xd0, row 2 interior top line; a second, shorter line starts filling row 4 by +40f and stabilizes by +60f, e.g. front_yard's second line reached 12 characters and stopped -- consistent with a 'place name' line followed by an 'owl message' line, matching the hint text's description). Verified via actual VRAM tile PATTERN bytes (the 16-byte 2bpp bitmap behind each tile ID, not just the tilemap's tile-ID numbers, which can coincidentally match across runs due to a monotonic per-session glyph-slot allocator starting at the same base index every time) -- reproducible byte-for-byte across two independent re-runs of the same checkpoint (0/28 tile patterns differ). Also reproduced in villager_screen (a second decorated room) and shop_screen (an undecorated room, confirming this box isn't tied to the decorated-room rendering quirk above) -- all three show the same box mechanic, with DIFFERENT content per room (front_yard vs villager_screen: 18/28 tile patterns differ; shop_screen's first line is shorter, 14 characters, and no second line had started by +90f). This had never been seen before because every prior probe (this session's own first broad matrix included) tapped :a for only 2-4 frames -- far short of the ~20 frames needed for the typewriter effect to even begin.
REFUTED (specifically, the d-pad-cursor claim): tapping or holding each of the 4 directions (2f, 10f, and continuous 20f) before the :a hold, across front_yard and villager_screen, produced byte-IDENTICAL VRAM tile pattern data to the no-direction baseline at every duration short enough not to leak into real gameplay (<=~14 frames total) -- the text box's content never changed with direction. Durations long enough to matter (~20f continuous) leaked into real Link movement and cancelled the map screen outright (reverted fully to the raw closed-gameplay tilemap, room_id unchanged), the same already-documented leak artifact above, never producing an in-overlay cursor effect. No evidence of a d-pad-movable cursor was found in the input space actually tested.
Most consistent reading: :a reveals a real per-room info box (plausibly about the room where you were standing when you opened the map), not a freely-cursor-navigable browser of OTHER rooms' info as the hint text literally describes -- but this isn't certain, since an untested input pattern (e.g. moving the d-pad AFTER the box is already open, to page between entries) could still exist. The fixed 'you are here' marker (interior row10/col2) stayed in the same cell throughout, unmoved by any of this session's input, consistent with the existing INCONCLUSIVE note above -- still not confirmed to be a cursor. Text glyphs were not decoded to actual characters (no font/OCR tooling in this repo) -- only that a real, room-specific, reproducible text render exists is established, not what it says.
What NOT to redo: the exact input space tested here (tap/hold of all 4 directions, 2f/10f/20f durations, front_yard + villager_screen, verified via VRAM tile pattern bytes not tilemap IDs) -- re-testing the same durations/rooms will just reproduce this null result. A genuinely different approach (cursor movement AFTER the box opens rather than before; or decoding the glyphs to read what the box actually says) is the open question, not this one.
FOURTH CHECK, September 9 2026 (owner-directed reproduction, same session): the text IS trivially human-readable once the hold runs long enough for the typewriter effect to finish -- no OCR/font tooling needed, just export the framebuffer at the right frame. From lib_front_yard.dump: select delay=25f (not the ~20f estimate above -- worth retuning that number if this becomes load-bearing), then hold :a for 70f total, reads plainly as "Chez Marine" (French, i.e. "At Marine's place" -- Marine/Marin is a known Link's Awakening character). This is a real place-name/landmark label, matching the hint book's description exactly. ALSO NEWLY VISIBLE at this longer hold: the fixed 'marker' (interior row10/col2) is not a plain dot -- it renders as a 4-directional arrow cluster around a center point (up/down/left/right arrows), strongly suggestive of an actual d-pad cursor icon, not just a position pin. This does not contradict the earlier 'never moved under tested input' refutation -- every direction test in that pass happened BEFORE pressing :a; moving the d-pad while the text box is already open (the subagent's own proposed next question, immediately above) is still untested and now looks like the more promising input pattern given what this icon actually looks like.
FIFTH SESSION, September 9 2026 (Explorer subagent -- the room-tileset-dependent grid/icon rendering hypothesis above, tested directly rather than just proposed): CONFIRMED for one pair, with a real complication from a second 'plain' room -- not a clean single confirm/refute. Recalibrated open-window timing for lib_front_yard.dump/lib_shop_screen.dump (select held continuously, not tapped): ~29f initial delay then a stable open window through ~74f (matches the prior ~20-25f delay / ~36f-open estimate); read at frame 50, well clear of both edges. Full BG-tilemap tile-ID scan, tilemap rows 0-17 x cols 0-31 (border ring + interior 16x16 body + icon/legend block), front_yard vs shop_screen: the border ring (col0 every row, row0 cols0-19: 0xfc/0x3b/0x52.../0x3c) and the interior body (rows1-16 cols2-17, uniform 0x2c) are tile-ID-identical in both rooms, and the registry-pinned icon region (rows6-9 cols20-31) is ALSO byte-for-byte tile-ID-identical in both (2c 2d 7c 7c 7c 7c 7c 7c 7c 7c 2a 2b / 7f 3d 7c 7c 7c 7c 7c 7c 7c 7c 3a 7f / 7f 7f 2c 2d 7c 7c 7c 7c 2a 2b 7f 7f / 7f 7f 7f 3d 3e 3f 3e 3f 3a 7f 7f 7f) -- extending the earlier front_yard/room177 icon-ID match to a third room pair, one of which is genuinely plain-rendering. Read raw 16-byte 2bpp CHR patterns (mmu.debug_read over 0x8000+id*16) for all 27 distinct tile IDs found across that whole region, in both rooms' open-window states: 23 are byte-identical between rooms; exactly 4 (0x75, 0x7c, 0x7e, 0x7f -- precisely the tiles used inside and just below the icon glyph) differ. Decoded to pixels: front_yard's 0x7c/0x7e/0x7f share one literal 16-byte pattern (00 ff 00 ff 24 ff 18 ff 18 ff 24 ff 00 ff 00 ff) rendering as a solid filled diamond/lens shape -- the actual icon body; shop_screen's pattern at those SAME three IDs is three different, unrelated-looking partial shapes, blank across their top rows -- textbook 'blank or draws something unrelated'. Clean, direct confirmation of hypothesis (a) for this pair: identical tilemap content, divergent VRAM graphics data, nothing chosen differently by the overlay itself.
THIRD-ROOM CHECK (room160_entry.dump -- an older Motherboard-format dump, loads fine after applying the documented @current_period_div_accumulator fix post-load; its open window lands at the same ~30-74f range) does NOT reproduce this clean picture. Border ring and interior body still match front_yard/shop_screen tile-for-tile (including the marker cell's own ID, 0x0c, though its surrounding decoration differs -- already covered by the INCONCLUSIVE note above, not re-litigated here). But the icon/legend block (rows6-9 cols20-31, the exact pinned region) is mostly DIFFERENT BY TILE ID, not just pattern: only 3 of 48 cells share front_yard's ID (row6 cols20-21 = 0x2c/0x2d; row7 col21 = 0x3d); the other 45 use a wide, unrelated set (0x2e, 0x2f, 0x6d, 0x48, 0x49, 0x5a, 0x7f, 0x3c, 0x3e, 0x3f, 0x74, 0x0c, 0x1c, 0x75...). Checked explicitly: even where an ID DOES coincide numerically with front_yard/shop_screen's set (0x7c, 0x7e, 0x7f, 0x75), room160's pattern at that ID matches NEITHER other room -- three-way distinct content at the same ID number (e.g. room160's 0x7c = 07 00 1e 01 3f 00 7f 00 7f 00 ff 00 ff 00 ff 00, matching neither front_yard's nor shop_screen's 0x7c bytes above). This gives byte-level confirmation to the already-recorded September 8 anomaly note ('room160... a completely different icon-region tile set') -- not a stale artifact, a real and reproducible fact.
Net verdict: MIXED, not a single clean (a)/(b) answer -- the two 'plain' rooms diverge from the decorated case in different ways. For front_yard/shop_screen specifically, (a) is the complete, confirmed explanation. For room160, the icon-block tile IDs themselves differ substantially (partial (b)), while the border+interior scaffolding -- the large majority of the scanned region, and the part of the overlay that actually reads as 'the grid' -- still supports (a)'s core claim that the overlay's layout logic (where the border/interior/icon blocks sit, and that the interior is a uniform undecorated 0x2c field even in the 'decorated' room) is room-independent. (French: 'Watch out for sea urchins!') -- confirming the spiky sprites nearby ARE the 'oursins' (sea urchins) it warns about. No OAM sprite found at the sign's own screen position (x~35-43,y~16-27) -- it is BG-tile art with an invisible position/facing-triggered interaction, same pattern as dialogues.house2_telephone_examine's invisible trigger. No dialogue-state change, no item, no HUD/inventory change (B-slot shield+N1, A-slot empty, hearts, rupee counter all identical before/after, screenshots diffed visually) -- this is NOT a progress/item indicator. Room otherwise not explored beyond the sign's immediate vicinity. The ground-accessible area is small and effectively enclosed: from the sign, routing south then east along the inside of the hedge's L-bend reaches a dead end where `Navigator.probe_all` reads `down: :blocked, right: :blocked, up: :ok, left: :ok` -- the room's own SW pocket, bounded by the hedge (north/west) and the diagonal-striped water/river texture (south/east). No room_id/map_id transition was found anywhere in this pocket this session (stayed 225/0 throughout). The water strip was never actually entered/crossed -- consistent with a swim-gated boundary (Link has no Flippers-equivalent item yet, A-slot empty per HUD) but this is a hypothesis, not confirmed by a direct swim attempt. A second attempted route -- hugging the top row east past the sign toward the bush cluster in the room's NE corner, looking for a gap there -- did not reach that area: repeated rightward `Navigator.move!` calls from just below the sign registered partial diagonal slides (net movement mostly downward, not east), never confirmed whether this is a real invisible obstacle or an artifact of the sign's own hitbox; genuinely unresolved, not exhaustively tested, a real gap for a future session. Additional room content found: a second sea-urchin OAM variant, attrs=0x43 (vs. the previously-recorded 0x03/0x23), at multiple positions along the hedge's south edge, plus a distinct green amphibious-looking OAM sprite sitting in the water strip itself (not approached or identified further) -- both out of this session's interaction scope. Unexplained damage: HUD hearts dropped from 3 full to 1 full across two movement batches in the hedge-corner pocket, with no OAM sprite read adjacent to Link in the snapshots taken immediately before/after either batch -- same 'hit lands inside move!'s internal multi-tap loop, invisible to a before/after snapshot' pattern flagged this session in room_labels['224/0'] for the same creature family; not root-caused, flagged only. Checkpoints saved for reuse, in path order from a fresh full-health entry: `lib_explorer_225_fresh_entry.dump` (x=23,y=26, 3 hearts) -> `..._225_route3.dump` (x=28,y=50) -> `...225_route6.dump` (x=42,y=86) -> `...225_route7.dump` (x=42,y=96, the dead-end pocket, 1 heart -- resume elsewhere if continuing, this one is low-health). NE ROUTE RESOLVED, September 10 2026 (independent Explorer subagent, this session's mandate): the previously-abandoned NE route (hugging the top row east past the sign, blocked by the old "diagonal slides") is NOT a wall -- it leads to a real, previously-undocumented room transition into 226/0 (see room_labels['226/0']). Root cause of the old diagonal slides finally isolated: TWO distinct hazards live in this NE strip, not one. (1) An invisible mobile hostile creature (same wandering-enemy pattern documented above in this entry and in DECISIONS.md's D11) delivers contact knockback plus damage mid-tap, inside a single Navigator.move! call's internal loop -- never visible in a before/after OAM snapshot, consistent with this project's already-established 'hit lands inside move!'s multi-tap loop' pattern. (2) Ordinary blocking terrain -- a sea-urchin OAM cluster (tile=0x5C/0x5E) and a flower-cluster BG obstacle -- also sits along this strip, independent of any creature. TACTIC TESTED (owner's suggestion): holding B (the equipped shield) continuously via mmu.joypad.key_state directly (keys.press(:b), directional taps without clearing b, keys.clear at the end) while pushing the same route that cost 3 hearts unshielded produced ONE full clean run (fresh_entry -> x=76,y=26) with hearts unchanged (20/20) the whole way -- real evidence the held shield blocks the invisible creature's contact knockback at least some of the time. NOT a universal fix though: a later shield-held attempt through the same general area (a down-right-up detour around the flower wall) still took a full heart of damage (20->16) with no OAM sprite visible adjacent in the snapshot immediately before/after -- so the shield mitigates but does not reliably prevent every hit in this room; treat 'B held' as risk-reducing, not risk-eliminating. WORKING ROUTE (a strategy, not a fixed tap count -- same caveat as every other route in this room cluster): from `lib_explorer_225_fresh_entry.dump` (x=23,y=26, B held throughout) -- down to y~42, east to x~51, back up to y~26, east to x~76 (a real wall here: a flower cluster's BG hitbox blocks further east at y=26-36, confirmed hard-blocked with zero position change across 4 separate move! calls, not a knockback). The fix is dropping further south than the first instinct suggests: south to y~41 (below the flower's hitbox but still above the sea-urchin row at y~50) clears it, then east resumes cleanly all the way to x~124 (the base of a second, NE-corner palm tree, itself a real wall blocking further east/north). From there, south along the tree's east flank to y~65-68, then east 3-4 more taps crosses room_id/map_id from 225/0 into 226/0 at x=17,y=67, hearts unchanged (16/20) on this final crossing. Checkpoints saved in path order (all shield-equipped/B-held, all after the point where hearts dropped to 16/20 except the first two): `lib_225_ne_shield_held_end.dump` (x=51,y=26, 20/20) -> `lib_225_ne_shield_continue_end.dump` (x=76,y=26, 20/20) -> [two failed detour branches NOT on the working path, kept for reference: `lib_225_ne_round_flowers_end.dump` and `lib_225_ne_careful_end.dump`, both dead-ended back at x=76,y=26, the first of the two losing a heart] -> `lib_225_ne_far_south_end.dump` (x=108,y=41, 16/20) -> `lib_225_ne_to_palm_end.dump` (x=124,y=41, 16/20) -> `lib_225_ne_under_palm_end.dump` (x=17,y=67, 16/20, already inside 226/0). hypothesis/verified_count 1 -- single session, single reproduction of the full route; the exact tap counts at each leg are almost certainly as tap-count-fragile as every other route already logged for this room cluster (see the south_exit entries in world_topology) -- only the strategy (which y-bands to route through, and to hold the shield) should be treated as durable, not the specific move! counts above.

Not explored past the entry snapshot: no signpost, chest, dialogue trigger, or further room transition was looked for this session, budget went to reaching the room itself. No HUD/inventory change observed on the crossing itself (hearts read 16/20 both immediately before and after, unchanged -- a clean crossing, not a hit). Checkpoint: `lib_225_ne_under_palm_end.dump`. Pushing that `up` cost two more hits in three moves (9->8->5->4 hearts, ~1 heart left) while sliding diagonally (x=61,y=60 -> x=36,y=28) despite only `:up` being pressed each time -- consistent with this room cluster's known 'knockback invisible in before/after OAM, lands inside move!'s internal tap loop' pattern (see room_labels['224/0'] and DECISIONS.md's D11), not a bug. `probe_all` at that point: `up: :blocked, down: :ok, left: :blocked, right: :blocked` -- a genuine dead end with only retreat open. Session STOPPED here (hearts at 4/20, one hit from a possible KO) rather than push further into this pocket; it was NOT exhaustively cleared -- the area past this cul-de-sac's `up` wall is unreached, not ruled out, for safety reasons, not because it was searched. No `bidule`/item/chest/signpost/dialogue trigger found anywhere reached this session (every screenshot taken along all 3 directions showed only palm trees, hedge, water strip, sea-urchin OAM sprites, and the hostile creature family -- no new object). Checkpoints in path order: `lib_226_up_end.dump` (dead end, 16/20) / `lib_226_left_end.dump` (crossed back to 225/0, 12/20) / `lib_226_right_end.dump` (x=61,y=60, 9/20) -> `lib_226_up2_end.dump` (x=36,y=28, 4/20 -- LOW HEALTH, the room's known-worst point so far) -> `lib_226_retreat_end.dump` (one step back toward safety, still 4/20, do not push further from here without a way to restore hearts). hypothesis/verified_count 1, single session. FOURTH PUSH, September 10 2026 (independent Explorer subagent, D12 amendment scope, HP-write permission exercised): resumed from lib_226_up2_end.dump (x=36,y=28, 0xDB5A=4/24, the prior session's safety-stop point in the NW cul-de-sac where probe_all read up/left/right all :blocked, down :ok only). Screenshots at this point show only palm trees, hedge, sea-urchin sprites and a green creature -- no item. A follow-up probe_all AT THIS SAME east-shifted position (x=36,y=26, 2px off the original x=36,y=28 read) found 'right' newly :ok where it had read :blocked before (the same narrow-gap-alignment pattern already known from house2_interior's/shop_screen's doors elsewhere in this project) -- pushed it (1 clean move, HP-write 16->24 beforehand since 2 hearts felt low enough to risk stopping short again) to x=46,y=26, near the room's NE palm tree, no damage on this particular push. probe_all there: up STILL :blocked (4th independent confirmation of this same north wall, at 2 different x columns now), down/left/right :ok. CONCLUSION: the 'up' wall bounding this room's NW/N edge is real and consistently reproduces -- not a stopped-early artifact of the prior session's safety floor, and not the narrow-gap kind of false wall found elsewhere. No 'bidule'/item/chest/signpost found in any screenshot taken this push. Per the anti-patch rule (3 identical :blocked results at the same column, plus a 4th at a different column, all consistent), this specific wall is closed as a genuine room boundary -- a future session wanting more of this room should try the remaining unexplored ground past x=46,y=26 (right/down still read :ok there) instead of re-probing 'up' again. HP-writes this push: 0xDB5A 4->24 (resume from prior session's 1-heart stop) and 16->24 (before the right-push retry, 2 hearts remaining) -- both on scratch checkpoints (lib_226_*.dump chain), never main.dump, per D12's Plage Coco amendment. Checkpoints in path order: lib_226_explore_start.dump (24/24) -> lib_226_up_retest.dump (16/24, wall reconfirmed) -> lib_226_final_safe.dump (16/24) -> lib_226_right2_end.dump (24/24, x=46,y=26) -> lib_226_session_end.dump (24/24, this session's final safe resting point). hypothesis/verified_count 1, single session. D13 PRIMITIVE SWEEP, September 11 2026 (independent Explorer subagent, using Navigator.avoid_hostiles_and_push!/avoid_hostiles_and_move! as the PRIMARY method throughout, radius:16 shipped default, no manual retuning needed this session): resumed from lib_226_session_end.dump (x=46,y=26, HP 24/24, probe_all up:blocked/down,left,right:ok) -- state reconfirmed to reproduce exactly before pushing further. Route: (1) pushed right, clean x=46->91 (zero hazards seen, 4 damage total) then continued right x=91->124 where a REAL WALL was found and reconfirmed -- 10 total :blocked results at the exact same position (x=124,y=26) across two separate avoid_hostiles_and_push! batches plus a clean, full-HP, hazard-avoidance-free probe_all re-check, zero net position drift throughout (not a knockback/hazard artifact, a genuine boundary); (2) healed (HP-write, see below) and pivoted to `down` from that same wall point -- real south progress, x=124,y=26 -> x=119,y=59 (4 damage), where `down` itself became newly blocked but `right` opened up again; (3) pushed right from there, x=119->154,y=59->58 (12 damage, up to 3 hazards seen at points), landing in a genuine 3-way cul-de-sac (up/down/right all :blocked, only `left`, i.e. back the way in, open) -- reconfirmed clean via a fresh probe_all at full HP after another top-up; screenshot there (lib_226_154_reconfirm.png) shows the pocket bounded by dense water on its remaining sides, consistent with the water strip already known from 224/0/225/0; (4) separately, pushed `up` from the x=119,y=59 point (previously only probed :ok, never pushed) to check for a hidden side-branch between the two explored rows -- it does NOT lead anywhere new: after a few real steps it lands back at the EXACT SAME wall coordinate already found in step (1), x=124,y=26, confirming this whole area is one single contiguous pocket, not two separate zones. CONCLUSION: the entire 'past x=46,y=26' area this room's mandate asked about is now closed -- bounded east by the x=124,y=26 wall, south/southeast by the x=154,y=58 water cul-de-sac, and the two routes rejoin rather than opening further ground. No `bidule`/item/chest/signpost/dialogue trigger found anywhere: 7 screenshots taken across the whole route (checkpoint chain: e226_start_reconfirm, e226_right_batch1/2/3/4, e226_down_batch1, e226_up_from_59_end, plus e226_154_reconfirm) show only the already-catalogued palm trees, hedge corner, water/river diagonal-stripe strip, sea-urchin sprites (tile=0x5C/0x5E), and the tile=0x60-family hostile creature -- pixel-diffed to confirm the frames are genuinely distinct (not a stale/frozen render) despite visually similar repeating tile patterns; color histograms confirm this room renders in the same 4-shade DMG-style palette as every other checkpoint checked, so no icon/item would show as an out-of-palette color, only as an unfamiliar tile shape -- none was seen. D13 PRIMITIVE ASSESSMENT (second validation data point, a different room from its first 209/0 retest): the shipped `radius:16` default worked as the primary method with NO retuning needed here (unlike 209/0, where the original 40px default had to be abandoned first) -- it correctly told genuine walls (many consecutive :blocked calls with zero position drift, hazards_seen frequently 0) apart from real hazard-blocked pushes (nonzero hazards_seen, position sometimes still advancing), and reached real new ground both south and further east. `avoid_hostiles_and_push!`'s `min_hp: 8` floor triggered 3 times as designed, each requiring a caller-driven HP top-up to continue (never automatic, per D13's own design intent). HP-writes this session: 3, all on scratch checkpoints only (`e226_*.dump` chain, never `main.dump`), all logged with old/new values and cause at the time: 8->24 (after batch2, before retrying the y=26 wall once more to confirm it), 12->24 (after that wall was confirmed, before pivoting to `down`), 8->24 (after the SE cul-de-sac was reached, before a clean full-HP reconfirm probe). hypothesis/verified_count 1, single session.

Two independent columns, same wall + same knockback pattern -- 'up' is closed as a real boundary in this west portion of the room, not chased a 3rd time. background_tilemap_predicts_walkability.method: Read the active BG tilemap (hardware.bg_tilemap_0/1, selected by hardware.lcdc bit 0x08, via mmu.debug_read to bypass PPU bus-gating) and map cell (row,col) [= world y/16, x/16, the oracle grid's own convention] directly to the 2x2 tile-ID block at tilemap rows {2*row,2*row+1}, cols {2*col,2*col+1} -- no SCX/SCY scroll correction applied or needed in either sampled state (both had SCX=SCY=0).
background_tilemap_predicts_walkability.finding: In both rooms, every oracle-confirmed-walkable cell's 2x2 tile-ID block and every oracle-confirmed-blocked-target cell's block partition into two disjoint sets with zero full-block overlap: starting_house (37 walkable / 18 blocked cells) uses ~2 floor signatures vs ~9 wall signatures; front_yard (25 walkable / 8 blocked cells) uses 6 floor/path signatures vs 2 wall signatures. The partition is per-room/per-tileset categorical, not a single global numeric threshold across rooms (no 'tile ID >= 0x80 means solid' rule holds in both) -- likely a ROM-side per-tile-ID lookup table keyed by tileset, not a per-room WRAM buffer. Supersedes wram_unmapped.room_object_grid's WRAM-buffer hypothesis: the signal exists, just in the wrong memory region from what Session 1 searched.
caveats: Granularity: a couple of single tile IDs (0x0A/0x0B, 0x7F in starting_house) appear in both a walkable and a blocked 2x2 block, but only at genuine doorway/wall-base boundaries where a 16px oracle cell straddles an 8px tile boundary -- collision plausibly resolves at 8x8 tile granularity, not the 16x16 cell grid the oracle/Navigator use. Not a contradiction of the finding, but means a literal cell-level lookup needs care at boundaries.

Directional asymmetry: front_yard cell (6,3) has the room's own unambiguous wall tile signature ({0C,0C,1C,1C}), yet Koholint::Navigator.move! reached it via a LEFT approach and reported the (5,3)<->(6,3) boundary open from below -- while the static oracle recorded (5,3)'s 'down' edge as blocked. Read as a one-way ledge (walkable from one side only), not a refutation -- but means a pure tile-ID lookup alone won't fully replace directional probing without also encoding one-way edges.

SCX/SCY=0 held in every state sampled this session (both checkpoints, plus after 8 real moves in front_yard), but front_yard is a scrolling room -- the no-scroll-correction formula is unverified further from the door/spawn area and should be re-checked before relying on it room-wide.

CONFIRMED, verified_count 2 (owner visual report + Explorer session, September 9 2026): the bottom row (screen-relative row 8, y=128-143) is the game's HUD/status bar, not real world terrain. Checked 5 rooms (front_yard, villager_screen, screen3_north, overworld_screen2, shop_screen) by reading LCDC/WY/WX from their checkpoints directly: all 5 have window_enabled=true (LCDC bit 5), WY=128, WX=7 -- the PPU window layer covers y=128-143 across the full screen width in every case, confirmed visually in 3 exported PNGs (B-item slot, A-item slot+count, rupee counter, hearts). RoomClassifier/Terrain.signature_at reads the BG tilemap underneath the window, which is a different address space than what's actually drawn there -- so row 8's 'signature' is incidental BG data, not the visible HUD and not real terrain, and produces meaningless walkable/blocked noise (e.g. villager_screen row 8: cols 2-3 cached 'walkable', cols 4-9 'blocked', despite the whole row being the same opaque HUD on screen). Fix (not yet implemented): exclude row 8 from walkability BFS/grids, gated on each room's actual WY/window-enabled state rather than a hardcoded '8', as a guard against a future room placing its window differently. All 10 existing walkability JSONs need regenerating once this lands -- their current row-8 entries are noise.

CONFIRMED, verified_count 2 (owner visual report + Explorer session, September 9 2026): the same visual object (e.g. a tree) can carry a DIFFERENT tile-ID signature depending on which room/tileset it's in -- this is the mechanism behind what the owner observed as 'identical tiles categorized differently' in the Atlas overlays. Explorer investigation ruled out both alternative explanations by direct evidence: (a) classifier reuse across rooms -- read all 8 generation scripts in scratchpad/walkability/, every one instantiates a fresh RoomClassifier per room (map_room.rb:38, local variable, one run_room call per room); (b) a within-room caching bug -- RoomClassifier#verdict_at is a plain Hash memoization keyed on the exact signature array, no code path exists for one signature to yield two verdicts in one instance's life, confirmed both by reading lib/terrain.rb:43-49 and by an instrumented empirical run on front_yard (Module#prepend logging every verdict_at call: 71 calls, 12 distinct signatures, 0 within-room conflicts). The per-room partition is working exactly as D8 designed it -- not a bug -- but nothing surfaced this to a reader comparing overlays across rooms, which is how it read as an inconsistency. Fix (not yet implemented): state the per-room-locality explicitly in each walkability JSON's 'note' field and in the Atlas legend, so cross-room comparison isn't misread as a defect. Secondary, unconfirmed mechanism flagged by the same Explorer session: RoomClassifier's unit is a 2x2-tile-ID block, not a single visual tile, so two screen positions with an identical individual graphic could in principle land in different 2x2 groupings and get different (correctly cached, non-conflicting) verdicts -- no concrete instance isolated yet, would need tile-ID-to-rendered-graphic correlation, out of scope so far.

Owner-confirmed, September 9 2026, NOT YET INVESTIGATED: terrain in this game is not uniformly static. At least two categories exist: (a) cosmetically modifiable but walkability-invariant (plain grass -- can be cut, stays walkable before and after), and (b) modifiable WITH a walkability change (bushes -- currently read as 'blocked' by every terrain classification so far, but per the owner, passable once cut, presumably by a sword Link doesn't have yet). This means 'blocked' in the current D8 model conflates two genuinely different things: a permanent boundary (a real wall, water) and a conditional one (an obstacle that stops being a wall once Link has the right item/action). No classification done so far distinguishes these -- a real open question for how the world model should represent walkability once inventory starts to matter.

CONFIRMED, September 10 2026 (owner-prompted atlas check): the walkability model is entirely blind to sprite/OAM-based obstacles, not just conditional terrain. crate_room's walkability overlay shows all 9 of its known-physical crate/book-stand objects (confirmed OAM sprites, tile=0x58, not BG tiles -- see visual_catalog.crate_room_book_objects) as uniformly walkable, because RoomClassifier only ever reads the BG tilemap underneath them -- the floor tile there genuinely is plain walkable grass, and nothing in the current model checks whether a static OAM sprite sits on top of it. Not limited to crate_room -- any room with a static sprite-based obstacle (as opposed to BG-tile terrain like a wall or bush) will have the same false-walkable gap. Distinct from the mobile-creature case (D9 tracks those separately, by position, not by walkability) -- this is about STATIC sprite obstacles the BFS/grid has no way to see at all.

FIRST DIRECT CONTACT/INTERACTION TEST, September 10 2026 (isolated Explorer subagent, falsifiable-question mandate: what actually happens on bush contact / :a-while-facing-a-bush, never tested before -- every prior 'blocked' classification came from D8's BG-tilemap signature method alone, never a live interaction probe). Method: lib_shop_wide3.dump (shop_screen/179-0, x=60,y=112, full HP 24/24, an existing yard checkpoint from the door-approach sessions), nudged to y=106 (1 move! call), then 10 RAW Koholint::Navigator.tap(:right) calls (not move!'s internal up-to-8-tap aggregation, to see true per-tap behavior) toward a bush cluster confirmed visually adjacent to Link in the rendered framebuffer (round dark-green cluster graphic, same style as the room's known flower-bush ring per room_labels['179/0'] -- this specific cluster sits near the yard's SW dead-corner, ~x=64-68,y=106, NOT the exact x=81-94 door-approach cluster pixel-mapped above, which remains unreached by any on-file checkpoint per this entry's THIRD SESSION note; reaching that exact cluster would mean a 4th door-routing attempt, already closed off by the anti-patch rule -- this test used the nearest reachable instance of the same BG-tile-classified terrain type instead, staying inside this session's budget). RESULT, unambiguous: all 10 raw taps produced dx=0,dy=0 -- zero net displacement, not even a partial sub-tile slide or bounce, identical every single tap. HP (0xDB5A) stayed at 24/24 throughout. Then 3x Navigator.tap_button(:a) (project-standard TRIGGER_FRAMES=2/SETTLE_FRAMES=28 timing) plus 120 extra idle frames, framebuffer rendered after each press and compared pixel-by-pixel against both the pre-press frame and a known real dialogue-box reference screenshot from the same room (lib_shop_dialogue_done.dump, the yard NPC's save-tip box -- a large bordered text rectangle, unmistakable): none of the bush-contact frames show any dialogue box, text, or UI change -- the only pixel differences (~1100-1200px, scattered across the whole screen, not the dialogue box's rectangular footprint) are ordinary background/idle animation (leaf/bush sway, a distant ambient sprite near the shop roof, far from Link's position), not a reaction to the press. A post-:a Navigator.move!(:down) still worked normally (real movement away from the bush), confirming no stuck/soft-lock state either. CONCLUSION: bush contact and :a-while-facing-a-bush both match option (a) exactly -- plain-wall behavior, zero movement, no message, no detectable side effect of any kind, at least for this cluster. No sound-only cue could be ruled out (no audio inspection tooling in this project), but every other observable (position, HP, framebuffer, subsequent movement) is unchanged. Consistent with, not yet proof of, the standing 'conditionally-blocked, needs a cutting item' hypothesis -- this test only rules out (b)/(c) from that hypothesis's own falsifiable framing today, it does not confirm what a cutting item would do (Link has none to test with). verified_count stays 1 (single session); a future session retesting at the exact x=81-94 door cluster, or after obtaining a cutting item, would be genuinely independent checks.
